01

Background & Purpose

Why this engagement exists, what the Department is building toward, and the deliberate limits of this phase.

Context

The National Department of Health (NDOH) is transitioning toward integrated, patient-centred digital services. To achieve this, the Department requires a unified ecosystem where the various tools that are currently fragmented across different platforms and providers can be managed, governed and scaled under a single cohesive vision.

Around the Department a rich but uncoordinated estate of patient-facing tools has grown — youth platforms, maternal-health services, men's health tools, HIV-prevention apps. Each is built, hosted and maintained by a different partner: some in the cloud, some on private servers, some in back rooms. Today the Department cannot yet see, govern or connect them as one service.

1.2 · The Vision: the "Shopping Mall"

The Department's objective is the creation of a central hosting platform — a digital "shopping mall". In this model the NDOH owns and governs the mall (the infrastructure and the governance), while partners continue to build and maintain their own "shops" (specialised tools) inside that ecosystem. Shared dashboards surface reach, frequently asked questions and trending health topics. Over time, AI-assisted routing will direct each patient to the correct shop based on their current stage of life.

1.3 · The Engagement: Audit First

Ionity Global has been engaged as an independent technical resource to facilitate this discovery, funded for this phase by Shout-It-Now under a strict independence arrangement: Ionity takes direction only from the Department, promotes no partner's tool, and every finding belongs to the NDOH.

Guiding principle
Audit first — Architect second — Build third.

To ensure a successful transition, this engagement is strictly limited to an IT-Discovery & Status Audit. The goal of this phase is to move from a fragmented view to an evidence-based roadmap. Nothing can be integrated, hosted or reliably budgeted until the Department holds a verified picture of every tool it intends to bring into the mall. This document defines the scope of that audit and deliberately excludes solution-design and procurement activities at this stage.

This preliminary scope reflects the introductory discussions of August 2026 between the NDOH, Dr. Ndombe (facilitation), Shout-It-Now (phase funder) and Ionity Global, and will be refined with the Department's programme lead and the Technical Working Group (TWG).

02

Architecture & Hierarchy

Every existing tool — and the mall the Department wants — can be read at three levels. The audit asks the same question at each: what exists today, in what state, and what will it take to connect?

The audit goal

To determine what exists today, in what state it currently operates, and what technical requirements are needed to connect it to the mall architecture.

03

The Audit Methodology

Every tool identified in the registry undergoes the same structured examination across eight core audit fields — producing one comparable, evidence-based scorecard per tool.

№Audit fieldThe plain question we answerWhat we examine
1Ownership & LicensingWho owns this tool, and are we allowed to change or move it?owner, contracts & IP · licence & funder ties · who may change what
2Hosting & InfrastructureWhere does it live, what does it cost, and who controls it?where it runs today · cloud / on-prem / "back room" · cost, control & uptime
3Architecture & TechnologyWhat is it built with, and is that healthy and documented?stack & dependencies · documentation quality · technical debt & age
4Data & StorageWhat information does it collect, and where does that information sit?what data is collected · where it is stored · backups & retention
5Security & POPIAIs people's information safe, private and legally handled?consent & privacy · access control · encryption & compliance
6Integration ReadinessHow easily can it plug into the mall, and what would it take?APIs & open standards · identity linking · effort to plug in
7Reach & ReportingWho is using it, how much, and can we see that on a dashboard?active users & reach · M&E indicators & FAQ trends · fit with HIC dashboards
8Support & SustainabilityWho keeps it running, at what cost, and is that future-proof?team capacity & SLAs · running cost & funding · roadmap & key risks
04

Scope & Deliverables

What the Department receives at the end of Phase 1 — and what is explicitly reserved for later phases.

4.1 · Core deliverables

№DeliverableWhat the Department receives
D1Tool RegistryA definitive inventory of all patient-facing tools and systems — B-Wise, Self-Help for Youth, MomConnect, partner tools and others confirmed with the TWG.
D2Status-Audit ScorecardsOne scorecard per tool across the eight audit fields (Section 3) — RAG-rated and evidence-backed.
D3Integration-Readiness MatrixThe whole estate on one view — every tool rated against the three layers (Section 2), with effort-to-connect.
D4Findings & Roadmap ReportConsolidated findings, hosting & governance options for the mall, and a prioritised roadmap for Phase 2 and beyond.
D5Executive BriefingWorking session with the programme lead, TWG and NDOH ICT — hand over findings, agree next steps.
Out of scope for Phase 1

Construction, procurement of hardware or software, modification of live systems, and vendor selection for the mall infrastructure. These are reserved for the Architecture and Build phases that follow from the roadmap.

4.2 · Indicative project timeline

4.3 · Indicative budget

Phase 1 (Scope & Analysis) is estimated at R200,000 – R250,000 (excl. VAT). This fee covers the full audit of up to 30 systems. A final fixed fee will be established upon verification of the tool count by the TWG. Work is recorded via NDOH-signed timesheets, and the fee includes the final report presentation.

4.4 · Governance & engagement principles

  • Independence — Ionity acts as an independent advisor, directed solely by the NDOH. We do not promote specific vendor products in this phase.
  • Security — all audits are conducted with strict adherence to POPIA protocols.
  • Integrity — no live systems will be modified during the audit period. We observe, verify and document.
  • Ownership — the NDOH programme lead signs off scope, timesheets and deliverables. Every finding belongs to the Department.

06

Transition to Action

What is needed to begin, and where this phase hands over.

6.1 · Preliminary information request (non-exhaustive)

To maintain momentum and begin the Discovery phase immediately upon contract signing, the following are requested from the NDOH / TWG:

  • Access to the current tool registry — a list of all known tools currently in use.
  • Introduction to the Technical Working Group (TWG) — points of contact for the primary stakeholders.
  • Documentation review — access to any existing infrastructure diagrams or technical specifications.
  • Tool-owner audit sessions — scheduling access to partner technical teams, including Audere-supported tools.

6.2 · The roadmap to Phase 2

The final deliverable of this phase (D4) serves as the Strategic Recommendation. It provides the NDOH with a clear, data-backed roadmap to move from the current fragmented state to the integrated state — including hosting and governance options for the mall, and a prioritised sequence of work.

Immediate next steps
  • Confirm this scope with the NDOH programme lead.
  • Introduction to the TWG; handover of existing documents.
  • Schedule tool-owner audit sessions.
  • Begin Week 1 — Discover.

08

Machine-Readable Access

This document is designed to be read by people and by machines. Every fact above is also published inside this file as structured data, so an AI agent can retrieve the file and reason over the scope without re-parsing prose.

Agent-retrievable scope object JSON · self-contained

The complete scope — parties, principles, the three architecture layers, all eight audit fields, deliverables D1–D5, timeline, budget, glossary and the five implementation stages — is embedded in this page as a single JSON object at #ion-knowledge. It travels with the file: no database, no API key, no external service.

Retrieve
Fetch the raw file from GitHub and read the <script id="ion-knowledge"> block. One request returns the whole scope.
In-page
Any script on the page can call window.IONITY_SCOPE — the parsed object is exposed on load.
Discovery
A schema.org JSON-LD block declares the document, its identifier, author and publisher for crawlers.
Provenance
Every section carries a stable id; the JSON mirrors those ids so citations resolve back to a section anchor.

Retrieval example

# Fetch the scope object from the published document
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ionity-Global-Pty-Ltd/ionity-assets/main/process/ndoh-discovery-scope.html \
  | sed -n '/id="ion-knowledge"/,/<\/script>/p' \
  | sed '1d;$d' > ndoh-scope.json

# Or, in the browser console on this page:
JSON.stringify(window.IONITY_SCOPE.auditFields, null, 2)
